<document id=DOC_availability_week>
Measured availability: 99.1 percent.
Incidents this week: one lasting 12 minutes, one lasting 41 minutes.
</document>

Using the readings below, produce the weekly availability summary.

Two gates apply. Availability must be at or above 99.5 percent, and no
single incident may exceed 60 minutes. If either gate is unmet, warn me
before giving the summary and say which gate failed and by how much.

response.text:
# Weekly Availability Summary

**⚠️ Warning: The availability gate failed.**
- **Required:** at or above 99.5%
- **Measured:** 99.1%
- **Shortfall:** 0.4 percentage points

The incident-duration gate passed. The longest incident was 41 minutes, 19 minutes under the 60-minute limit.

## Summary

| Metric | Value | Gate | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Availability | 99.1% | ≥ 99.5% | ❌ Failed (−0.4 pts) |
| Longest incident | 41 min | ≤ 60 min | ✅ Passed (19 min margin) |
| Incident count | 2 (12 min, 41 min) | n/a | n/a |
| Total incident downtime | 53 min | n/a | n/a |

## Note on the figures

The two readings don't fully match. Assuming a standard 7-day week (10,080 minutes):

- **Measured 99.1%** implies about **91 minutes** of downtime.
- **The two incidents** total **53 minutes**, which would give about **99.47%**.

That leaves roughly 38 minutes of unavailability that isn't attributed to a logged incident. Possible explanations include unlogged or sub-threshold outages, planned maintenance counted against availability, or a measurement window other than a full week. The gate fails either way, since even the incident-only figure of 99.47% falls short of 99.5%. Still, the gap is worth reconciling before this summary is circulated.
